name: IR2110STRPBF
title: IR2110/IR2113 high and low side MOSFET and IGBT gate driver, 500 V or 600 V
summary: A gate driver for one high side and one low side N-channel MOSFET or IGBT, each output with its own input. The high side output sits on a floating, bootstrap-supplied channel that may ride up to 500 V (IR2110) or 600 V (IR2113) above the power return. Each output sources and sinks 2 A minimum (2.5 A typical) from a 10 V to 20 V gate supply; the logic side runs from its own 3.3 V to 20 V supply and its ground may sit up to 5 V either side of the power return. Both channels have undervoltage lockout, a shutdown input turns both outputs off, and the two channel delays agree within 10 ns (IR2110) or 20 ns (IR2113). It comes in a 14-lead PDIP and a 16-lead wide-body SOIC (S suffix).

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: One IR2110 drives a high side and a low side N-channel MOSFET, each through a series gate resistor, with the load connected between the two switches' outputs. The high side switch's drain goes to the bus, up to 500 V (IR2110) or 600 V (IR2113), decoupled to ground by a capacitor. A diode from VCC to VB and a capacitor across VB and VS form the bootstrap supply of the floating HO stage. VCC is decoupled to COM and VDD to VSS. HIN, SD and LIN come from the controller; COM ties to the low side switch's source and ground.

parts.value: bus, up to 500 V or 600 V

circuits.title: Floating supply voltage transient test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit that slews VS faster than 50 V/ns to test the floating channel's dV/dt immunity. VDD and VCC run from 15 V, decoupled by 10 µF and 0.1 µF; HIN, SD, LIN, VSS and COM are grounded. A 10KF6 diode from VCC charges a 0.1 µF bootstrap capacitor across VB and VS. VS connects to the HV supply (10 V to 500 V or 600 V, 100 µF bulk) through a 200 µH inductor with a 10KF6 diode across it, cathode to HV; an IRF820 MOSFET, driven by a pulse through a buffer, switches VS to ground, and a second 10KF6 runs from ground (anode) to VS. HO and VS are watched as outputs; LO is left open.

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the dynamic characteristics are measured in. VDD and VCC share one 15 V supply, decoupled by 10 µF and 0.1 µF; VSS and COM go to ground. A separate 15 V floating supply sits between VB and VS, decoupled by 0.1 µF and 10 µF, and VS is raised anywhere from 0 to 500 V or 600 V, decoupled to ground by 10 µF. Each output drives a load capacitance CL (1000 pF), HO to VS and LO to ground, and HIN, SD and LIN are driven from outside.

VS, - of the floating supply, 0 to 500 V/600 V

operation.text: Two independent output channels. LO is referred to COM and powered from VCC. HO is referred to VS and powered from VB, a floating supply built for bootstrap operation, so it can drive an N-channel MOSFET or IGBT in the high side position. The floating channel works with VS up to 500 V (IR2110) or 600 V (IR2113), tolerates VS going negative in a transient, and is immune to dV/dt up to 50 V/ns.

HIN, LIN and SD are CMOS Schmitt-trigger inputs, each with a pull-down, accepting CMOS or LSTTL output levels, down to 3.3 V logic. Their thresholds and currents are referred to VSS, the logic ground, which has its own supply VDD (3.3 V to 20 V) and may be offset from COM by up to ±5 V. The input thresholds scale with VDD (figures 12B and 13B).

HO follows HIN and LO follows LIN, in phase. While SD is high both outputs are held low. Shutdown is edge triggered, cycle by cycle: an output cut off by SD stays low after SD returns low and turns on again only at its input's next rising edge. The high and low side delays agree within 10 ns (IR2110) or 20 ns (IR2113).

Both channels have undervoltage lockout: one on VBS for the high side and one on VCC. The VBS lockout releases at 8.6 V typical rising and trips at 8.2 V typical falling; the VCC lockout releases at 8.5 V and trips at 8.2 V typical (limits in the static table).

Each output stage is a buffer for large current pulses, designed to keep cross-conduction inside the driver small: 2.0 A minimum, 2.5 A typical source and sink into a short for pulses up to 10 µs at 15 V bias. With 1000 pF load the outputs rise in 25 ns and fall in 17 ns typical.
The most negative VS the high side tolerates goes further below COM as VBS rises (figure 36), and the most positive VSS offset the logic tolerates grows with VCC (figure 37); both are typical curves.

Junction temperature rises with switching frequency and bus voltage, and depends on the switch driven. Figures 28 to 35 give it for IRFBC20 (RGATE 33 Ω), IRFBC30 (22 Ω), IRFBC40 (15 Ω) and IRFPE50 (10 Ω) at 10 V, 140 V and 320 V, VCC = 15 V, in both packages.
The top carries the part number, a date code, a lot code, an assembly site code, the IR logo and a pin 1 identifier. A P in the marking code position marks a lead-free released part.
